content: If I have a functor F which relies on some input like Monoid G, and I proved an instance i1 on it but then later under stricter condition (e.g Group G), I proved a stronger instance i2 which implies i1, does that mean I'm going to have a diamond on i1 when taking Group G?

Usually the anwwer is no; I think what you're asking is whether (F.instGroup instGroupG).toMonoid = F.instMonoid instGroupG.toMonoid holds, which entirely comes down to whether you implement F.instMonoid and F.instGroup correctly

The most common way this can go wrong is if in instMonoid you manually specify an npow, but in instGroup you accidentally tell lean to just use the default instead of inheriting the field from the monoid structure
You can check if with_reducible_and_instances rfl proves the two instances are equal.
